page.layout: One printed page, single column of running text, with a short italic verse couplet set below the paragraphs; no marginal notes. Page number at the head right. Catchword "Sequi-" at the foot right, signature "Ii 4" at the foot.

main_text.p: 7. Dextra pars mundi Geographis dicitur orientalis, Siniftra vero occidentalis: nonnullis vero dextra pars dicitur Meridies, Siniftra, Septentrio.

Dextrum & finiftrum in cœlo & terra relatiue dicitur respectu manus dextræ ac finiftræ in homine: nam si faciem homo vertat versus aliquam cœli plagam, neceffariæ ei vna plaga ad dextram erit, altera ad finiftram, tertia versus ipfam faciem, quarta à tergo. Itaque cum aliam cœli plagam respiciant alii artifices pro diuerso fuo fcopo, fit vt hæc aliis, aliis illa cœli pars Dextra aut Siniftra vocetur: nam Poetæ propter infulas Fortunatas faciem vertunt ad occasum, ideo Poetis plaga feptentrionalis eft dextra, meridionalis finiftra.

Aftronomi faciem vertunt versus meridiem, ideo illis plaga occidentalis eft dextra, orientalis finiftra. Geographi nonnulli dicunt fe faciem vertere ad feptentr. propter polum articticum, ideo illis orientalis pars mundi eft dextra, occidentalis finiftra. Sacerdotes faciem vertunt ad ortum, quod & augures olim faciebant, ideo illis meridies eft ad dextram feptentrio ad finiftram secundum vfitatos versus.

p.i: Ad boream terra, fed cœli menfor ad auftrum,
Prato Dei exortum videt, occasumq; Poeta.

main_text.p: Intermediæ plagæ funt, quæ à cardinalibus plagis declinant, fiue quæ mediæ funt inter cardinales plagas, nempe inter ortum & meridiem, inter ortum & fept. inter occasum & merid. inter occasum & fept. vel contra inter fept. & ortū, inter fept. & occasum, inter merid. & ortum, inter meridiem & occasum.
De his theorema eft: Geographi 12. plagas intermedias, nautæ vero 28. constituunt, quas plagas diuerfis ventorum nominib. infigniunt, vt in compaffo nautico ad oculum videre licet.

page.notes: Printed in an old typeface; the "I" of "Ii 4" is the gathering signature. The couplet is set in italic. Some words are uncertain in the scan, notably "fit vt" and "Sacerdotes" which are read as printed. The page is shown with a dark binding edge and show-through at the right, which are not transcribed.
